content: 1. Evidence from Indonesia suggests that the availability of healthcare services significantly impacts maternal and newborn health outcomes. (Studies in Family Planning, 2009; 40(1): 27–38). 2. Fullerton, Killian, and Gass (2005) evaluated the outcomes of communityand home-based interventions aimed at promoting safe motherhood and newborn care. Their findings were published in Health Care for Women International (2005; 26: 561–76). 3. Gabrysch et al. (2009) explored the cultural adaptation of birthing services in rural Ayacucho, Peru, highlighting the importance of tailoring healthcare services to local cultural contexts (Bulletin of the World Health Organization, 2009; 87: 724–9). 4. Ganju, Khanna, Taparia, and Hardikar (2014) emphasized the role of report cards in promoting accountability for maternal health, as detailed in the COPASAH Communique (2014; 8: 3–5, 33). 5. Gaym, Pearson, and Soe (2012) reviewed three decades of experience with maternity waiting homes in Ethiopia, demonstrating their effectiveness in improving maternal health outcomes (Ethiopian Medical Journal, 2012; 50(3): 209–19). 6. The GRADE Working Group developed a system for assessing the quality of evidence and the strength of recommendations, which is critical for WHO guidelines on maternal and newborn health interventions (accessed January 7, 2015). 7. Guyatt et al. (2008) discussed the importance of evidence quality in shaping WHO recommendations for health promotion interventions targeting maternal and newborn health (BMJ, 2008; 336(7651): 995–8). 8. Harkins et al. (2008) documented the health benefits of social mobilization through community-based Integrated Management of Childhood Illness programs in Peru and Honduras (Promotion and Education, 2008; 15(2): 15–20). 9. Hodgins et al. (2010) tested a scalable community-based approach to improve maternal and neonatal health in rural Nepal, with promising results published in the Journal of Perinatology (2010; 30(6): 388–95). 10. Hodnett et al. (2002) conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effectiveness of nurses as providers of birth labor support in North American hospitals (JAMA, 2002; 288(11): 1373–81). 11. Hodnett, Gates, Hofmeyr, and Sakala (2013) reviewed the benefits of continuous support for women during childbirth, as published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews (2013; CD003766). 12. Hofmeyr et al. (1991) investigated the impact of companionship during labor on clinical outcomes, labor progress, and breastfeeding success (British Journal of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, 1991; 98: 756–64). 13. Hossain and Ross (2006) examined the effects of addressing both demand and supply for emergency obstetric care in Dinajpur, Bangladesh (International Journal of Gynecology and Obstetrics, 2006; 92(3): 320–8). 14. Hounton et al. (2008) assessed the impact of a skilled care initiative on pregnancy-related mortality in rural Burkina Faso (Tropical Medicine and International Health, 2008; 13 Suppl 1: 53–60). 15. Hussein et al. (2012) conducted a systematic review on the effectiveness of emergency obstetric referral interventions in developing countries (PLoS Medicine, 2012; 9: 1–12). 16. Jewell and Russell (2000) evaluated the effectiveness of minority health coalitions in increasing access to prenatal care through early pregnancy projects (Journal of Community Health Nursing, 2000; 17(2): 93–105). 17. Julnes (1994) analyzed the outcomes of community-based perinatal care programs for disadvantaged adolescents, focusing on the Resource Mothers Program (Journal of Community Health, 1994; 19(1): 41–53). 18. Kaseje et al. (2010) highlighted the importance of evidence-based dialogue with communities to improve district health system performance (Global Public Health, 2010; 5(6): 595–610). 19. Kaufman, Liu, and Fang (2012) demonstrated the effectiveness of participatory planning in improving reproductive health in rural China (Global Public Health, 2012; 7(8): 856–68). 20. Kelly et al. (2010) evaluated the role of maternity waiting areas in reducing maternal mortality and stillbirths among high-risk women in rural Ethiopia (BJOG, 2010; 117(11): 1377–83). 21. Kumar et al. (2008) conducted a cluster-randomized controlled trial to assess the impact of community-based behavior change management on neonatal mortality in Shivgarh, Uttar Pradesh, India (The Lancet, 2008; 372: 1151–62). 22. Langer et al. (1998) investigated the effects of psychosocial support during labor and childbirth on breastfeeding, medical interventions, and maternal well-being in a Mexican public hospital (BJOG, 1998; 105(10): 1056–63). 23. Larsen and Muller (1978) studied obstetric care in rural South Africa, emphasizing the challenges faced by underserved populations (South African Medical Journal, 1978; 54(27): 1137–40). 24. Lee et al. (2009) reviewed strategies linking families and facilities for care at birth to reduce intrapartum-related deaths (International Journal of Gynecology and Obstetrics, 2009; 107 Suppl 1: S65–85). 25. Lewycka et al. (2013) evaluated the impact of women’s groups and peer counseling on maternal and child health outcomes in rural Malawi (The Lancet, 2013; 381: 1721–35). 26. Lungu et al. (2001) assessed the effectiveness of bicycle ambulances and community transport plans in strengthening obstetric referral systems in Southern Malawi (International Journal of Gynecology and Obstetrics, 2001; 12(2): 16–8). 27. Manandhar et al. (2004) demonstrated the positive effects of participatory interventions with women’s groups on birth outcomes in Nepal (The Lancet, 2004; 364(9438): 970–79). 28. Marsiglia et al. (2010) designed the Familias Sanas intervention to increase postpartum visit rates among Latinas (Journal of Health Care for the Poor and Underserved, 2010; 21(3): 119–31). 29. Marston et al. (2013) conducted a systematic review on the effects of community participation in improving the uptake of skilled care for maternal and newborn health (PLoS ONE, 2013; 8(2): e55012). 30. McPherson et al. (2006) evaluated the effectiveness of birth-preparedness programs in Nepal, with findings published in the Journal of Health, Population, and Nutrition (2006; 24(4): 479–88). 31. Mushi et al. (2010) assessed the effectiveness of community-based safe motherhood promoters in improving obstetric care utilization in rural Tanzania (BMC Pregnancy and Childbirth, 2010; 10: 14). 32. Panaretto et al. (2005) studied the impact of a collaborative shared antenatal care program for urban Indigenous women in Australia (Medical Journal of Australia, 2005; 182(10): 514–9). 33. Tripathy et al. (2010) evaluated the effects of participatory interventions with women’s groups on birth outcomes and maternal depression in India (The Lancet, 2010; 375: 1182–92).
